collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager tries to count who owes whom favors on a stick: keep counting, or throw the stick away.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (name1) has decided to work out, once and for all, who in the village owes (him/her) favors and whom (he/she) owes. (He/she) has a stick and a lot of time. (He/she) starts making marks. One for the fish (he/she) gave away. One for the roof somebody fixed. One for the baby (he/she) watched. One for the soup (he/she) was brought when (he/she) was sick.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: After about ten marks (name1) gives up, throws the stick in the fire, and goes to help a neighbor carry water. (He/she) doesn't mark it down. It feels much better not to. (He/she) has a feeling the village has been running this way for a very long time without anyone keeping count, and doing just fine.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (name1) counts for hours. The marks get very complicated. Someone owes (him/her) a fish, but (he/she) owes them a pot, but they borrowed (his/her) knife, but (he/she) ate their mango. At last (name1) sits back and looks at the stick, covered in marks. (He/she) laughs. Everyone owes everyone. It's not a debt. It's a village.
